items.title: Section: Diligence and Means Close Yogic Practice — Sixteen Components in All

items.zh: 精進有四。何等為四？一、為聞精進，二、為思精進，三、為修精進，四、為障淨精進。為聞精進者，謂為聽未聞，聞已究竟，勤心勇猛審決加行。為思精進者，謂如所聞法，獨處空閑，思惟其義，籌量、觀察。為修精進者，謂入寂靜，於時時間勤修止觀。為障淨精進者，謂於晝夜策勵精勤經行、宴坐，從諸障法淨修其心，勤心勇猛，審決精進。方便有四。謂尸羅律儀增上力故，善守其念；善守念故，能無放逸，防護其心，修諸善法；無放逸故，心正於內修奢摩他、增上慧法毘鉢舍那。此四瑜伽有十六種。當知此中，初由信故，於應得義深生信解；信應得已，於諸善法生起樂欲；由樂欲故，晝夜策勵，安住精勤、堅固、勇猛；發精進已，攝受方便，能得未得、能觸未觸、能證未證，故此四法說名瑜伽。
items.en: Diligence is fourfold: diligence for hearing, diligence for reflection, diligence for cultivation, and diligence for purifying obstruction. Means is fourfold: through the strength of discipline, one guards mindfulness well; through guarding mindfulness well, one becomes free of negligence, protecting one's own mind and cultivating wholesome states; through freedom from negligence, the mind rightly cultivates, within, both calm-abiding and the insight of higher wisdom. These four components of yogic practice, in sixteen forms altogether: first, through faith, one comes to deep confidence regarding what is to be attained; having such confidence, aspiration for wholesome states arises; through that aspiration, one exerts oneself day and night, abiding diligent, firm, and courageous; having generated diligence, one takes up the means by which what is not yet attained is attained, what is not yet touched is touched, and what is not yet realised is realised. This is why these four factors are called yogic practice.

items.title: Mental Engagement Opens: Forceful and Interrupted Operation

items.zh: 云何作意？謂四作意。何等為四？一、力勵運轉作意，二、有間運轉作意，三、無間運轉作意，四、無功用運轉作意。云何力勵運轉作意？謂初修業者，令心於內安住等住，或於諸法無倒簡擇，乃至未得所修作意，爾時作意力勵運轉。由倍勵力折挫其心，令住一境，故名力勵運轉作意。云何有間運轉作意？謂得所修作意已後，世出世道漸次勝進了相作意，由三摩地思所間雜，未能一向純修行轉，故名有間運轉作意。
items.en: What is mental engagement? It is fourfold: forceful operation, interrupted operation, uninterrupted operation, and effortless operation. What is forceful mental engagement? It is that of a beginning practitioner, causing the mind to abide and evenly abide inwardly, or to discriminate phenomena without distortion, up until the mental engagement one is cultivating has not yet been attained — at that time, mental engagement operates forcefully. What is interrupted mental engagement? It is that which, after the mental engagement being cultivated has been attained, gradually advances through the mundane or supramundane path beginning with the mental engagement of identifying the characteristic — still interspersed with reflective thought within concentration, not yet flowing in wholly uninterrupted practice. This is why it is called interrupted operation.

items.title: Section: Eight Kinds of Mental Engagement Complete

items.zh: 云何無間運轉作意？謂從了相作意已後，乃至加行究竟作意，是名無間運轉作意。云何無功用運轉作意？謂加行究竟果作意，是名無功用運轉作意。復有所餘四種作意。一、隨順作意，二、對治作意，三、順清淨作意，四、順觀察作意。云何隨順作意？謂於所緣深生厭壞，起正加行，而未斷惑。云何對治作意？謂能斷惑。云何順清淨作意？謂心下蹙，取淨妙相策令歡悅。云何順觀察作意？謂觀察作意。由此作意增上力故，順觀煩惱斷與未斷。
items.en: What is uninterrupted mental engagement? It is that which runs from after the mental engagement of identifying the characteristic through to the mental engagement of the culmination of applied effort — this is called uninterrupted operation. What is effortless mental engagement? It is the mental engagement that is the fruit of the culmination of applied effort — this is called effortless operation. There are, further, four other kinds of mental engagement: conforming, counteracting, inclining towards purity, and inclining towards observation. Conforming mental engagement is generating deep revulsion towards the object and undertaking correct effort, without yet having cut off affliction. Counteracting mental engagement is that which is actually able to cut off affliction. Inclining-towards-purity engagement is, when the mind sinks low, taking up a pure and wondrous image to rouse it to gladness. Inclining-towards-observation engagement is observational mental engagement — through its power, one accurately observes whether affliction has, or has not yet, been cut off.

items.zh: 問：於所緣境正作意時，思惟幾相？答：四。何等為四？一、所緣相，二、因緣相，三、應遠離相，四、應修習相。所緣相者，謂所知事同分影像明了顯現。

items.title: The Causal Characteristic: Resources, Eight Discursive Thoughts, and Mutual Causation

items.zh: 因緣相者，謂三摩地資糧積集，隨順教導，與修俱行猛利樂欲，於可厭法深生厭患，能審遍知亂與不亂，他不惱觸。或人所作，或非人作，或音聲作，或功用作。若毘鉢舍那而為上首，內略其心，極猛盛觀後因緣相。若奢摩他而為上首，發起勝觀，極猛盛止後因緣相。
items.en: The causal characteristic is: the accumulation of the provisions for concentration; conduct according with instruction; intense aspiration accompanying practice; deep revulsion towards what should be shunned; the ability to thoroughly discern disturbance from its absence; and freedom from external disturbance. … Where insight practice leads, calm-abiding — the mind gathered inward — is the causal characteristic following an intensely vivid observation. Where calm-abiding leads, an excellent insight arising is the causal characteristic following an intensely vivid stillness.

items.zh: 應遠離相復有四種。一者、沈相，二者、掉相，三者、著相，四者、亂相。沈相者，謂由所緣相、因緣相故，令心下劣。掉相者，謂由所緣相、因緣相故，令心高舉。著相者，謂由所緣相、因緣相故，令心於境起染、起著，作諸惱亂。亂相者，謂由所緣相、因緣相故，令心於外馳散擾動。
items.en: The characteristics to avoid are, further, of four kinds: sinking, agitation, attachment, and scattering. Sinking is when, through some fault in the object or the causal conditions, the mind becomes weak and low. Agitation is when, through some fault in the object or the causal conditions, the mind becomes elevated and restless. Attachment is when, through some fault in the object or the causal conditions, the mind gives rise to defilement and clinging towards the object, generating disturbance. Scattering is when, through some fault in the object or the causal conditions, the mind races and stirs outward.

blocks.text: The rest of "yoga", then **attention** (作意): four ways the mind can work in meditation. These four correspond to the nine stages of mental abiding met on Day 224.

"Diligence is fourfold: for hearing, reflection, cultivation, and for purifying obstruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: among obstructions, the afflictive is the main one. **Means**: through faith, deep confidence in what is to be attained; through discipline, mindfulness well guarded; and so on. Master Cháng Bǎi: discipline, mindfulness, non-negligence support one another.

items: **Forceful**: at the start, "until the attention one is cultivating has been attained", the mind must be held with effort.
**Interrupted**: the attention is there, but scattered moments break in.
**Uninterrupted**: from identifying the characteristic to the culmination of application.
**Effortless**: "the fruit of the culmination of application", running by itself.

blocks.text: The treatise adds further kinds: "inclining towards purity" (when the mind sinks, take up a pure, uplifting image to rouse it); "conforming" (deep revulsion towards what should be abandoned, and correct effort); and others.
The provisions for concentration, conduct according with instruction, intense aspiration, deep revulsion. Calm and insight are mutually causal. Venerable Miào Jìng: calm leads; insight follows.
**Sinking** ("the mind becomes weak and low"); **agitation**; **attachment**; **scattering** ("the mind races outward"). Venerable Miào Jìng: those with heavy desire are prone to agitation.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of diligence, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 審 in 審決?
options: hearing, reflection, cultivation, purifying obstruction; 審 is having studied earnestly until clear
quiz.why: "Diligence is fourfold: diligence for hearing, diligence for reflection, diligence for cultivation, and diligence for purifying obstruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: 審 means having studied very earnestly until it is clear; only then does one resolve to practise.

quiz.q: Of the obstructions purified by the fourth diligence, which does Venerable Miào Jìng call most important?
options: affliction, karma, and suffering are all obstructions, but the afflictive one is the fiercest and most important
quiz.why: "Diligence for purifying obstruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: among all these obstructions, the afflictive obstruction is the fiercest and most important. Practising calm and insight is to purify the mind, not to gain powers.

quiz.q: What are the four means, and how do the masters relate means to diligence?
options: Cháng Bǎi: discipline, mindfulness, non-negligence, calm and insight; Miào Jìng: means is really still part of diligence
quiz.why: "Through the strength of discipline, one guards mindfulness well." Master Cháng Bǎi: discipline, mindfulness, non-negligence, and calm and insight are the four means of accomplishing yoga. Venerable Miào Jìng: "means" is really still a matter within diligence.

quiz.q: How long does forceful engagement last, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "the mental engagement being cultivated" is?
options: until it is attained — access concentration; sitting seven days or seven years without it doesn't count
quiz.why: "Up until the mental engagement one is cultivating has not yet been attained — at that time, mental engagement operates forcefully." Venerable Miào Jìng says this is access concentration: whether you sit seven days or seven years, you are not counted among those with mental engagement until it is attained.

quiz.q: Effortless engagement is the fruit of the culmination of effort. Has affliction been cut, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: on the worldly path, desire's activity merely stops; the seeds remain — this is the first absorption
quiz.why: "What is effortless mental engagement? It is the mental engagement that is the fruit of the culmination of applied effort." Venerable Miào Jìng: it merely stops the active manifestation of desire; the seeds of desire remain — this is the worldly path.

quiz.q: What is inclining-towards-purity engagement, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say the "pure and wondrous image" is?
options: when the mind sinks, take a pure image to gladden it — recollecting Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, precepts, giving, and the heavens
quiz.why: "Inclining-towards-purity engagement is, when the mind sinks low, taking up a pure and wondrous image to rouse it to gladness." Venerable Miào Jìng: this is recollecting the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, precepts, giving, and the heavens — joy arising from the virtues of the Three Jewels.

quiz.q: What are the four characteristics to avoid, and who is prone to agitation, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: sinking, agitation, attachment, scattering; those heavy in desire tend towards agitation, those heavy in delusion towards sinking
quiz.why: "Sinking, agitation, attachment, and scattering." Venerable Miào Jìng: those with heavy desire are prone to agitation; earlier he says those especially heavy in delusion are prone to sinking.
